run.question: My AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 has high latency issues. Investigate why.

report.summary: The requested entity — AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 — does not exist in the target this Run could query. The connected target is a single-node kind Kubernetes cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, providerID kind://docker/opspilot-m1/...) whose only payment-related workload is the otel-demo 'payment' Deployment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), a different entity from the named Lambda function. No AWS/CloudWatch data source is available in this Run, so the runbook's CloudWatch steps (Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, CloudWatch Logs) could not be executed at all. The two observability backends that could have shown latency inside the cluster were also unavailable: every Prometheus-backed call and every Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no duration, error-rate or span-latency series could be read. Kubernetes state that could be read shows the otel-demo payment Deployment 1/1 ready and its pod running and ready, and the 60 newest payment log lines (06:36:36Z–06:54:27Z) show charge requests followed by 'Transaction complete' about 1 ms later at level info with no error lines; that is an observation about payment's own handler output, not an end-to-end latency measurement, and it does not address the reported Lambda latency. The flagd-config ConfigMap defines paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, both with defaultVariant 'off'. No root cause can be named: the fault the user reports is on a platform (AWS Lambda/us-east-1) that this Run has no access to, and the in-cluster latency signals could not be read.

claims.text: The only node in the target is 'opspilot-m1-control-plane', kubelet v1.37.0, OS 'Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)', providerID 'kind://docker/opspilot-m1/opspilot-m1-control-plane' — i.e. the target is a local kind Kubernetes cluster, not an AWS account or region.

The cluster's namespaces, in full (7 returned, not truncated), are: default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo. No namespace belonging to an AWS/Lambda workload is present.
Across all namespaces (32 pods processed), the only pod whose name contains 'payment' is payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d; no Kubernetes pod named 'payment-processor' was returned.
In namespace otel-demo there is a Deployment named 'payment' using image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment with spec.replicas 1, status.readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1.

Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6, node opspilot-m1-control-plane) is phase Running with container ready=true, restartCount 1, last terminated reason 'Unknown', and startTime 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z.

The 'payment' Deployment's container configuration contains no AWS/Lambda-related settings: its env holds OTEL_SERVICE_NAME (from the pod label), OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME=otel-collector, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=cumulative, PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317 and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (service.namespace=opentelemetry-demo, service.version=2.0.2, opspilot.integration.id=m0-otel-20260909); resources only set limits.memory=120Mi on container 'payment' exposing containerPort 8080.

The 60 newest log lines of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, covering 2026-11-21T06:36:36.679Z to 06:54:27.240Z (60 of 184 matching lines shown, limit reached), are all level 'info' pairs of 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with a transactionId, e.g. trace_id 5584534e23291d2132276af5285b9e33 at 06:36:36.679535Z completed at 06:36:36.680503Z and trace_id 2c85d4b3a71fa3fdcb2a07dfbfe14e54 at 06:54:27.238964Z completed at 06:54:27.240244Z; no error or warning lines appear in the shown slice.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) in namespace otel-demo defines a flag 'paymentFailure' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED, variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off, defaultVariant 'off') and a flag 'paymentUnreachable' (description 'Payment service is unavailable', state ENABLED, variants on/off, defaultVariant 'off'); it contains no latency/delay-injection flag for payment (delay-style flags present are kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, all defaultVariant 'off').

The Kubernetes Service 'payment' in namespace otel-demo maps port 8080/tcp-service to targetPort 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, and it is the only Service whose name matches 'payment' (26 services processed).

The high latency the user reports is most plausibly attached to the named AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1, which is a different entity from the otel-demo Kubernetes 'payment' Deployment/Service observed in this cluster; nothing in this Run observed that Lambda function, so its latency cause remains unknown.

A possible reason why every metrics query failed in this Run is the state of the read-only Prometheus proxy path: pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn shows restartCount 3 with last terminated reason 'Error' (container nginx), and all Prometheus-backed tool calls (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. This is an unverified hypothesis about the observability path, not about the user's Lambda, and it is not tied to the reported latency.

Rejected for the otel-demo 'payment' entity as far as this Run can see: that its feature flags are injecting payment faults/latency. flagd-config's paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable both carry defaultVariant 'off', and the payment pod's 60 newest log lines are completed charge/transaction pairs with no error or warning lines — no fault injection against payment is visible in these two sources. Flag runtime state (as changed through flagd at incident time) could not be read, so this rejection covers only what was readable.

Obtain CloudWatch access for the named function and run the runbook's steps as written: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics for Duration (Average/Maximum), InitDuration (Average/Count) and ConcurrentExecutions (Maximum), plus aws logs filter-log-events on the function's log group — none of these could be executed in this Run because no AWS/CloudWatch integration is connected.

Restore the target's Prometheus/Jaeger read path (the pod-level symptom is prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn with 3 restarts, last terminated reason 'Error') and re-run duration/error queries such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and app_payment_transactions_total, so that in-cluster latency can be compared to a baseline instead of being left unknown.

gaps: No AWS/CloudWatch integration is available in this Run (available data sources are jaeger, knowledge and kubernetes; not_integrated: change_history). Lambda Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions and CloudWatch Logs for 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 therefore could not be queried at all — the runbook's steps 1–5 could not be carried out, and the tool missing is the AWS CloudWatch / CloudWatch Logs integration.

The exact named entity 'payment-processor' was not found under that name anywhere I could look: a name filter over all pods (32 objects) returned no such object, and the payments-related objects present are the Kubernetes Deployment/Service/pod 'payment' in namespace otel-demo — a different entity, reported here as such rather than as the Lambda function.

Every Prometheus-backed call returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (metrics_range_query for traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"}, execute_prometheus_instant_query for 'up', get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total's service_name, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target for job 'prometheus'), so no latency, error-rate or label coverage could be read; those series are unknown, not zero.

Every Jaeger call returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, and traces_search for service 'payment' over 05:56:14Z–06:56:14Z), so no span durations, error spans or call chains exist in this Run; the parent-child topology of any payment call is unknown.

Kubernetes events across all namespaces returned zero items in the authorized window (status no_data), so no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Unhealthy/rollout evidence for the window is available; absence of events here is not evidence that nothing happened.

The cause of the restartCount 1 / lastState.terminated.reason 'Unknown' observed on payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (and on nearly every other pod started 2026-11-20T16:32) could not be determined: no events were readable and no previous-container logs were returned for the payment pod (the previous instance stream read 0 lines).

Flag runtime state is unknown: only the flagd-config ConfigMap defaults (all payment flags 'off') and payment's own logs were readable; whether flags were toggled via flagd during 2026-11-20T06:56:14Z–2026-11-21T06:56:14Z was not observable.
No change history is integrated in this Run, so no deployment/configuration change during the incident window can be confirmed or ruled out.

End-to-end request latency for the otel-demo 'payment' service was not measured by any available signal; the ~1 ms gaps between paired log lines describe the handler's own log timing only and are not a latency measurement or a baseline comparison.
next_steps: Connect an AWS CloudWatch/CloudWatch Logs data source for us-east-1 and repeat the runbook steps against function 'payment-processor' (Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, and [ERROR]/timeout log filtering) over the incident window.

Restore and verify the Prometheus read-only proxy and Jaeger backends so that traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and app_payment_transactions_total can be compared against a pre-incident baseline.

If the 'payment-processor' Lambda calls into this cluster's 'payment' Service or is otherwise backed by it, capture the baseline latency of the otel-demo payment Service before and during the incident so the two entities can be compared rather than assumed related.

content.name: lambda-performance-troubleshooting
content.content:
# AWS Lambda High Latency Troubleshooting

## Overview
This runbook helps diagnose and resolve AWS Lambda function performance issues including high latency, timeouts, and cold starts.

## Steps

### Step 1: Query Performance Metrics
Use CloudWatch to check Lambda function latency over time:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name Duration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 2: Check Function Logs
Look for errors or slow operations in CloudWatch Logs:
```bash
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --filter-pattern "[ERROR] OR [WARN] OR timeout" --limit 100
```

### Step 3: Analyze Cold Start Patterns
Query CloudWatch for cold start frequency:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name InitDuration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Count --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 4: Check Concurrent Executions
Verify Lambda isn't hitting concurrency limits:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name ConcurrentExecutions --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 60
```

### Step 5: Review Memory Utilization
Check if function needs more memory allocation:
```bash
aws logs insights start-query --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --start-time <epoch-start> --end-time <epoch-end> \
  --query-string "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @type = 'REPORT' | stats max(@maxMemoryUsed), avg(@memorySize)"
```
